To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose surrogate losses to cast SGD with self-tuned stepsize into an online convex optimization setting, (2) we prove that the surrogate losses are strongly convex with high probability and (3) we show that SGD with surrogate losses has a linear convergence rate that is self-adaptive to the level of the noise
we propose new surrogate loss functions to solve the problem of online learning the stepsizes in the stochastic optimization of non-convex functions.

(i) we cast the problem of tuning the stepsizes in SGD onto an online convex learning problem, (ii) we propose a new class of surrogate losses for online convex optimization, (iii) the resulting algorithm guarantees convergence rate that are automatically adaptive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a framework to automatically tune the learning rate of a SGD algorithm for non-convex optimization problems.
the following question: can we learn the optimal stepsizes in stochastic non-convex optimization in an online fashion without knowing the problem beforehand?

two main contributions: (1) a new surrogate loss that allows the use of online learning to solve the problem of tuning stepsizes for SGD; (2) an analysis of this approach that shows that the resulting algorithm converges at the optimal rate for non-convex stochastic optimization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the paper proposes a new surrogate loss function that can be used for online learning of step sizes for stochastic gradient descent in nonconvex optimization.
the proposed method can achieve a convergence rate that is automatically adaptive to the variance of stochastic gradients and that is optimal up to logarithmic factors.
we have proposed a new surrogate loss to cast the problem onto an online convex problem and then we have used no-regret online algorithm to solve the surrogate loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel surrogate loss to solve the problem of learning optimal stepsizes in stochastic optimization, which results in an algorithm that is adaptive to the level noise.
we have proposed a new surrogate loss for online convex optimization and used it to derive a self-tuning SGD algorithm with provably fast convergence rates in the non-convex setting.

we propose a new framework to solve a long-standing open problem in the stochastic optimization community: how to automatically learn the optimal stepsizes in SGD without any knowledge of the problem at hand?
The main takeaway from our work is that
surrogate losses can be used to cast many problems of interest in online learning onto the online convex optimization problem and thus can be solved using online convex optimization techniques.
the problem of learning optimal stepsizes can be reduced to a convex optimization problem and can thus be solved efficiently by existing online algorithms.
online learning is a useful tool to tackle the problem of tuning stepsizes in SGD.
